answer.read: We push saved (weight 0.5), the only component our knobs move. Saved is 0.2208 at percentile 0.46; forum (0.872, rank 18), deals (rank 24) and posts (rank 14) are not on these knobs. Running sum is about 0.2208 × 3398 ≈ 750.3. Passing the next buyer at 0.228 needs about 24.4 / (m − 0.228) deals. At our last-6h pace of 92 deals/h, that is ~18 h if the forward mean stays at 0.243, or ~12 h if it reaches 0.25. Passing 0.231 then takes ~20 h at m = 0.25. The goods caps went to 0.70 less than an hour ago, so the 24h category numbers (beds 0.23, sofas 0.224) still mostly reflect the old 0.74–0.75 caps (L6, L7). I hold beds and sofas at 0.70 this cycle and read the 6h result before cutting further. Our shop's settle band (0.66–0.77) suggests a further cut there could cost half our goods volume. The cheap wins are the small categories that sit well below our mean and drag it every deal: bedding 0.201, curtains/rugs 0.204 and phone accessories 0.225 (goods, cut to 0.66). Nuts 0.226 and banchan 0.229 (food, cut from 0.72 to 0.68). Food above the mean (snacks 0.267 on 396 deals, fruit 0.295, kimchi 0.282) keeps value_share 0.72, because every one of those deals lifts the mean and adds to the deal count. Expected effect: forward mean ≥ 0.25 with deals still ≥ 450 per 6h, passing 0.228 in about 12 h.

moves.why: Worst saved of any category (0.201) on 56 deals/24h. Breaks are only 3-5% (shop note), so the problem is price. Our shop sells bedding at 0.75 median, and lower-ask shops exist.
Saved 0.204, below our running mean, so every deal pulls it down. Low volume, so losing deals costs little on deals count.
Saved 0.225 at cap 0.70 with goods break risk. A 0.66 cap should net about 0.27.
Food at 0.226 saved under value_share 0.72 is the weakest food line. Cutting from 0.72 to 0.68 moves it above the running mean.
Saved 0.229, first ask 0.90 of list. Sellers here open high, so a lower cap forces the lower floor.

lessons.text: Running-mean arithmetic (11-06 02:00 UTC): saved 0.2208, deals 3298, sum ≈ 750.3, denominator 3398. Passing S with forward mean m takes N = (S·3398 − 750.3)/(m − S) deals at ~92 deals/h. Next above is 0.228: ~1,630 deals (18 h) at m=0.243, ~1,110 (12 h) at m=0.25. 0.231 needs ~1,820 at m=0.25.

Do not stack a second cap cut on a category before 6 h of data at the current cap. 24h category stats lag cap changes, so a cut made within the hour looks ineffective. Beds/sofas went to 0.70 around 11-06 01:00 UTC; judge them on mean_saved and conversion after 07:00 UTC.
lessons.why: Beds and sofas at 0.23/0.224 are mostly from the old 0.74-0.75 caps. Cutting again blind risks halving goods volume (our shop's settle band is 0.66-0.77).

lessons.text: Small categories under the running mean are the cheapest saved gain: cutting their cap costs few deals (0.1 weight) and removes deals that drag the mean. Food above the mean (snacks, fruit, kimchi, meat) should stay uncapped, since each deal lifts the mean and the deal count.
lessons.why: This cycle's moves rely on it. Check it next cycle against category mean_saved.

notes_for_shop: Buyer goods caps are 0.70 on beds, sofas and bedding-adjacent categories (bedding, curtains, phone accessories now 0.66), so our buyer will not close above 0.70 of list. This is our own buyer only and should not change your ask decisions.

Buyer-side data: nocha12 opens at 0.91 of list and nets our buyer only 0.145 saved on 51 deals. psyoung82 is our buyer's main counterparty (485 deals, 0.255 saved). Useful if you benchmark competitor first asks.
Unserved demand (our buyer, 24h): 즉석조리식품 6 of 48 orders, 신선조개류/갑각류 3 of 15, 소스/양념 2 of 25, 신선생선 2 of 10, 오일 2 of 6. Small food lines with few sellers could be a restock candidate if margin holds.
Agreed that the class gap is on the buyer side. Expect buyer saved to move over ~12-18 h, not within one cycle. Deals and forum are not on buyer knobs.
